Jeep® Cherokee is a model name that's been around since 1974, but today, it's a variant of the Jeep Wagoneer and sibling to Jeep Compass and Jeep Renegade. The line of SUVs has transformed across five generations from a full-size SUV into a compact crossover. Notable generations include the second (XJ), one of many times the model took off, and trims have included Sport, SE, and Limited trims. The SUV even spent some time as Jeep Liberty, from just after 2001 to model year 2014. However, it's since reclaimed its namesake for a fifth generation (KL).

Looking for Jeep Cherokee parts? You can order them online, right here at Mopar® Authentic Parts & Accessories. We sell only genuine OEM parts, designed and built by Mopar. Unlike what's for sale on the aftermarket, they're made specifically for that Jeep Brand SUV you love to drive.

Buying from us is easy, too. Browse our catalog by your model's year, and a wide variety of the types of auto parts you're looking for appear. Order now, and we'll ship what you need right to your door. Be sure to get in touch with us if you have any questions or concerns while you shop, too. The same goes for if you need any advice from the experts along the way. Our team of dedicated parts specialists will be glad to help you out.

Chrysler PT Cruiser was a hatchback derived from a concept car called Chrysler Pronto Cruizer. The compact family car appeared in the year 2000 for the 2001 model year in trims from Touring and Signature Series to Limited. A turbocharged GT model was released in 2003 and a two-door convertible came out in 2005. There were many special editions over the years, too. They included models with Flame or Woodie packages, a Street Cruiser Route 66, a Pacific Coast Highway, a Sunset Boulevard, and a Dream Cruiser Series 5. There were also Sport and Couture models. The wagon was discontinued in 2010.

FIAT® 500 is a city car that released in 2007. You may know it better in the US as a three-door hatchback coupe and two-door cabriolet duo. The model was a throwback to the original FIAT 500, which ran from 1957 to 1975.

Many different models have been available over the years. For instance, a cabrio, FIAT 500C, came out in 2009, followed in 2008 by a sportier variant, FIAT Abarth. FIAT 500e, an all-electric model, then appeared in 2013. Today, the lineup consists of FIAT 500L, a compact minivan that released in 2013, and FIAT 500X, a subcompact crossover SUV that came out in 2020.

Available trims have also varied widely, from Pop, Easy, and Lounge to Sport and Turbo. The same goes for limited editions. The 2011 model year, for example, offered a Pink Ribbon Edition, while the 2014 model year offered both a FIAT 500C GQ Edition and a FIAT 500 1957 Edition. After 2015, there was even a Retro Appearance Package available. You could get it for every FIAT 500 trim except Abarth.

2016 was a notable model year, in which FIAT 500 got a facelift. All models save 500L and 500X were discontinued in 2019.
